elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Inserted Subsection 5.2 d): "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, MSL will provide the transition assistance ..." — this cures the chapeau in 5.2 a), which was limited to "expiration or termination for default".

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: New clause d) commits only to "a period of at least ninety (90) Days following such expiration or termination"; no six-month assistance period appears anywhere in the operative text.

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
elements.evidence: Clause d) is silent on pricing; neither it nor Section 5.2 a) ii) contains any then-current-rates (or any charging) mechanic.

elements.element: Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Clause d): "within thirty (30) Days after such expiration or termination, export and deliver to IBM all data belonging to, supplied by or processed for IBM that is in MSL's possession or control." (Note: "Days" is defined at 1.3 as business days.)

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: Clause d) requires only that MSL "export and deliver" the data; no commonly used/machine-readable format requirement is stated, and Section 5.2 a) iii) speaks only of returning documentation and confidential media.

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: No deletion or written-certification obligation exists in clause d) or elsewhere in the cited termination provisions.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Clause d) opens "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason", so the assistance and export duties are not gated to default terminations.

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: Clause d) fixes the previously open-ended Section 5.2 a) ii) duty: "provide the transition assistance described in Subsection 5.2 a) ii) for a period of at least ninety (90) Days following such expiration or termination."

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Clause d): export and delivery of "all data belonging to, supplied by or processed for IBM" within thirty (30) Days after expiration or termination; the scope covers every category of IBM data, not selected types.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: the single inserted Subsection 5.2 d) supplies (i) an any-reason trigger, (ii) a committed minimum 90-Day assistance period anchored to the existing Section 5.2 a) ii) assistance scope, and (iii) a 30-Day export of all IBM data.

Preferred is not complete — four elements are absent from operative language: a six-month assistance period, a then-current-rates charging basis, a commonly used machine-readable return format, and post-return certified deletion. The finding correctly targets fallback only.

Minimality holds: one concise insertion, no deletion or paraphrase of existing Section 5.2 language, no survival tail, no at-own-expense or procedural extras, and no duplication of the existing 5.2 a) iii) return of documentation/confidential media (which is a different subject matter).

Intent preserved: clause d) supplements rather than contradicts the 5.2 a) default-only chapeau and 5.2 c) inventory buy-back; the cross-reference to "Subsection 5.2 a) ii)" resolves to an existing provision, leaving no dangling reference or undefined term.

Drafting caution (not a failure): "Days" is defined at 1.3 as business days, so the 30-Day export window runs roughly six calendar weeks and the 90-Day assistance period runs roughly eighteen calendar weeks. The usage is consistent with Section 5.2 a) iii) and the defined-term convention, but if a hard calendar deadline is wanted, change the export trigger to lower-case "thirty (30) calendar days".

Optional strengthening toward preferred, if leverage allows: add "in a commonly used, machine-readable format" to the export duty and a sentence requiring MSL thereafter to delete IBM data and certify deletion in writing; add "at MSL's then-current rates" only if the parties need an express charging basis.
